definition: A scale on which equal distances stand for equal multiplying factors, such as each gridline being $10$ times the one before, used when positive values cover a very wide range.

Taking logarithms of one or both variables so that curved data lie on a straight line: for positive data, $\ln y$ against $x$ is straight for an exponential model $y = ka^{x}$ and $\ln y$ against $\ln x$ is straight for a power model $y = kx^{n}$.
A graph with logarithmic scales on both axes, or of $\ln y$ against $\ln x$, on which data from a power model $y = kx^{n}$ with $k > 0$ and $x > 0$ lie on a straight line with gradient $n$.
A graph with a logarithmic scale on one axis only, usually the vertical one, on which data from an exponential model $y = ka^{x}$ with $k, a > 0$ lie on a straight line.
